legend: ✅ in the code · ⚠️ partial, or only on the provider side · ❌ none · 🔜 planned by the author, no code yet · — does not apply. Every cell was decided by reading the source of the project as of 2026-10-07, not its README; the column of @alexify/mailer is this repository as of 2026-10-18.

groups.title: Runtimes (from imports and CI, not run)

rows.title: Sending log on the provider side

deno.note: Through `npm:@alexify/mailer`. Deno’s `fetch` sends a request again when a reused connection closes before its answer, so the docs give it a `fetch` of its own ([known issues](/guide/known-issues#deno)).

failover.note: A failure after which the provider may have taken the message is marked `deliveryUnknown`: `./retry` does not retry it and `./pool` does not fail over with it.

retry.note: A failure after which the provider may have taken the message is marked `deliveryUnknown`: `./retry` does not retry it and `./pool` does not fail over with it.

rateLimit.text: token bucket per key, FIFO, shared store

queue.text: MongoDB outbox (transactional), BullMQ driver, memory queue
queue.note: Permanent failures fail at once, `Retry-After` is a minimum, and a delivery of unknown outcome is never sent blindly again; in MongoDB, a job is written in the transaction of its cause.

attachments.text: path, URL, data URI, stream, bytes, Blob
attachments.note: Nothing is read implicitly: `fromPath` and `fromUrl` are called by the application, `fromUrl` checks every redirect against `allowUrl` (no private address by default) and bounds time and bytes.

rawMime.text: SMTP, sendmail, JMAP, SES, Mailgun, SparkPost, Cloudflare

templates.text: 9 engines passed in: EJS, Handlebars, Pug, MJML, Liquid, Nunjucks, Eta, Mustache, React Email
templates.note: Names, never paths; locales, layouts, front-matter subjects, CSS inlined without remote fetches, text derived.

batch.text: native: Resend, Postmark, Mailjet, Mailtrap, JMAP; concurrency elsewhere

scheduled.note: A transport that cannot schedule refuses the message before sending it, rather than sending it at once.

proxy.text: SMTP: HTTP CONNECT or any `connect`; HTTP: `fetch`

verify.note: The other five have no request that checks a sending key without sending a message.

webhooks.note: A signature where the provider signs (SNS, Svix, ECDSA, HMAC), its Basic credentials or token where it does not; a window of time, and an id kept as taken only once the handler commits its events.

suppression.note: On the [roadmap](/guide/why#the-plan) of the reliability layer: designed, with no code yet.

auditLog.text: state model + sinks, MongoDB among them; crypto-shredding next
auditLog.note: Each state of a message, from the queue to the webhooks, one event per change, written once by its id. The keyed HMAC and encrypted recipients are on the [roadmap](/guide/why#the-plan).

streaming.text: SMTP yes; DKIM and SES buffer

proxy.text: HTTP CONNECT, SOCKS through a module

nodeMin.text: needs a connector of your own

apiCoverage.text: only mail/send typed; ~251 endpoints in USAGE.md

failover.text: multi-region endpoint on the AWS side

webhooks.text: SNS signature not in the SDK
